correctness.rationale: The proof constructs simple 0/1 edges via unique ordered and mixed differences, verifies connectedness and degree 2r²-r, and exactly factors the Hermitian Bloch adjacency as vv*−rI. The finite-root avoidance lemma is proved for arbitrary finite nonconstant F with F(0) and F(1) nonzero: choose M multiple of all unit-root orders and avoid finitely many forbidden M from non-torsion zeros. Thus P(z) and P(z^M) never vanish together, ensuring strictly positive uniform separation by compactness. The exact 15-regular spectral interval is established by an SOS identity, with equality at t=π and maximum at t=0. A fresh standard-library verifier exactly checks Laurent coefficients, sparse recurrence and small polynomial coprimality. Infinite statements are not inferred from finite checks.

originality.rationale: The mathematical distinction is strictly positive spectral separation for each negative-integer flat band in a two-site zero-one periodic graph, not the already known existence of those flat energies. A Laurent rank-one expression by itself permits band touching if both component polynomials share a unit-circle root; our new exponent-selection argument prevents that. Broad algebraic flat-band criteria and generic absence results do not directly supply the discrete all-integer isolated construction. Alternative indexing or equivalent constructions remain a residual novelty risk.

value.rationale: An isolated flat band is a qualitatively stronger spectral object than a possibly embedded or touching flat eigenvalue. The result gives such an isolated compact-localized band for every negative integer at or below -3 with only two sites per period, no edge weights or onsite controls, and bounded degree for each r. The sharp explicit 15-regular graph has exactly the full spectrum {-3} union [-1,15] and gap two. This resolves a structurally natural band-separation design question and is not a textbook restatement of the earlier nongapped existence construction; no claims about stability of exact flatness under general perturbations are made.
